doc.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

chapter: The Tonight Show and famous accompaniments
title: First day on the Tonight Show band and Jack E. Leonard
summary: Smith took the piano chair for Doc Severinsen and was insulted on camera by Jack E. Leonard on his first day.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Tell us a little more about working on the Tonight Show band.

Well it was a great experience. There again, as embarrassing moments — so I got the job, and that’s right Skitch Henderson had been the leader, but then there was some trouble there and he left, and Doc Severinsen, my good friend and a great trumpet player, and I was used to working with him in those days in the studios doing something. And he said, “Well I’m the band leader now,” you know, “I’d like you to do the job.” I said fine. So I show up. And you know you rehearse the music as much as you can, just once through, and then you sit there and the show goes on for an hour and a half and you play what you have to play. But then they come back after the commercial, and a couple of stage hands come up, take the piano away from me, put it right out in the center of the stage. Then he said, “get up.” I said, “What do you mean?” They take the piano seat and put it out there. So the camera comes back, and it’s just on me, in the center of the stage. The band’s over there. And this big fat comic comes out. [Jack E.] Leonard. Oh, he was very big at the time, it was kind of before Don Rickles, his whole act was to insult people. And very funny.
And you didn’t know this was coming?

No, no, I didn’t know this was coming. I didn’t know this from a hole in the wall. But he comes out there and proceeds to do like ten minutes on me. And I’m sitting there.
